# njlea

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/tor-gu/njlea/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tor-gu/njlea/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

njlea is a data package for R: a registry of New Jersey law enforcement agencies, from 2020.
It gives every agency a stable ID, its names over time, its level of government and
function, the municipalities it polices, its FBI ORIs, and every spelling of it used by the
NJ Office of the Attorney General (OAG) datasets.

It exists so that packages built on OAG data, such as
[njoagleod](https://github.com/tor-gu/njoagleod) (officer diversity) and
[njoaguof](https://github.com/tor-gu/njoaguof) (use of force), can identify agencies the same
way and be joined on `agency_id` instead of on names.

## Installation

You can install the development version of njlea from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("tor-gu/njlea")
```

## What's in it

```{r}
library(njlea)

get_agencies(2025) |> count(agency_level)
```

The registry covers every agency that appears in one of its sources: the OAG's Law
Enforcement Officer Diversity data (2021 and 2025 releases), use of force data, and Major
Discipline data. An agency that appears in none of them, or only in the FBI's lists, is not
included.

Five tables:

* `agency`: one row per agency and name. An agency keeps its `agency_id` when it is renamed.
* `agency_alias`: every spelling of every agency, exactly as each source writes it.
* `agency_municipality`: the municipalities each agency polices, by year, using
  [njmunicipalities](https://github.com/tor-gu/njmunicipalities) GEOIDs.
* `agency_ori`: the agency's FBI ORIs (the New Jersey State Police has 22; some agencies
  have none).
* `alias_source`: the sources behind `agency_alias`.

## Conventions

**IDs.** Agency IDs (`NJLEA0001`, …) are opaque. Once released, an ID is never deleted,
reused or repurposed.

**Years.** `first_year` and `final_year` give the years a row is *true* (the agency existed
under that name, or the link held), not the years a source reported it. The registry starts
in 2020, so `first_year = 2020` means "vouched for from 2020". `final_year = NA` means
current. A dated change counts in whole years: a rename takes effect in the year of its
effective date, and an agency that ends exists through the year of its last day.

**Level and function.** `agency_level` is the government that establishes and controls the
agency (Municipal, County, State, Bi-state, School district), or Private if none.
`agency_function` is what it does:

```{r}
agency |> distinct(agency_id, agency_level, agency_function) |> count(agency_function)
```

**County.** `county` is the agency's own county for Municipal, County and School district
agencies, and `NA` for State, Bi-state and Private ones.

**Names.** Municipal departments are named after their municipality, following the FBI's
convention ("Cherry Hill Township Police Department", "Absecon Police Department"). Other
agencies use their official names.

## Examples

#### Agencies in a year

`get_agencies()` returns the agencies in existence in a year, with their names as of that
year. `multi_municipal` is `TRUE` for an agency that polices more than one municipality.

```{r}
get_agencies(2025) |> filter(multi_municipal)
```

#### Finding an agency

`find_agency()` searches canonical names and every source spelling. Here a former name
finds the Youth Justice Commission, which was the Juvenile Justice Commission until
March 2025:

```{r}
find_agency("juvenile justice")

agency |> filter(agency_id == "NJLEA0539") |> select(first_year, final_year, agency_name)
```

#### Municipalities served

`get_agency_municipalities()` lists the municipalities each agency polices in a year. A
municipal department's own municipality is its `Home` link; a municipality it polices by
agreement is a `Service` link. Camden County Police Department polices Camden city, and
took over Woodlynne in 2024 when the Woodlynne Police Department disbanded:

```{r}
get_agency_municipalities(2025) |> filter(agency_id == "NJLEA0132")
```

Use `geoid_year` to get GEOIDs as of another year, as in
`njmunicipalities::get_municipalities()`. `geoid_year = 2000` gives the stable `GEOID_Y2K`
codes.

#### Resolving source spellings

`resolve_agency()` is for packages that build on OAG data: it maps each spelling, exactly as
the source writes it, to an `agency_id`. With `strict = TRUE` (the default) it stops on any
spelling it doesn't know, listing them all, so a new spelling is caught when the consumer
package is built.

```{r, error = TRUE}
resolve_agency("njoag-major-discipline", "Bergen",
               c("Bergen County Sheriffs Office", "Ridgefield PD"))

resolve_agency("njoaguof", "Bergen County", c("Bergen Co Sheriffs Dept", "Nowhere PD"))
```

`suggest_agency()` proposes candidates for a new spelling, and `check_agency_years()` checks
that each agency existed in the years a dataset reports it:

```{r, error = TRUE}
suggest_agency("Bergen", "Ridgewod Vilage PD")

check_agency_years(c("NJLEA0001", "NJLEA0001"), c(2023, 2019))
```

#### Joining to FBI data

ORIs are attributes, not keys. Join `agency_ori` to FBI Crime Data Explorer data on `ori`:

```{r}
agency_ori |>
  filter(agency_id == agency$agency_id[agency$agency_name == "Rutgers University Police Department"])
```

## Changes since 2020

Agencies that ended, or were renamed, during the period covered:

```{r}
agency |>
  group_by(agency_id) |>
  filter(n() > 1 | any(!is.na(final_year))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(agency_id, first_year, final_year, agency_name)
```

* Morris County Park Police merged into the Morris County Sheriff's Office on 2022-01-01.
* Woodbury Heights dissolved its department in July 2023; the City of Woodbury's police
  department took over.
* Brookdale Community College's police were replaced by the Monmouth County Sheriff's Office
  in 2023.
* Woodlynne's department disbanded on 2024-09-01; Camden County Police Department took over.
* Middlesex County College became Middlesex College on 2021-01-01.
* The Juvenile Justice Commission became the Youth Justice Commission on 2025-03-17.

Each change's source is in the `note` column.

## Known gaps

* **New Jersey State Police coverage.** The State Police is the local police of many rural
  municipalities (77 full-time and 24 part-time, according to a 2022 bill), but no published
  list names them, so it has no `Service` links yet. Most municipalities with no agency in
  `get_agency_municipalities()` are policed by the State Police, but not all:

  ```{r}
  njmunicipalities::get_municipalities(2025) |>
    anti_join(get_agency_municipalities(2025), by = "GEOID") |>
    nrow()
  ```

* **Agencies outside the sources.** Only agencies that appear in an OAG source are included.
  For example, Pine Valley had a small police department until it merged into Pine Hill in
  2022, but no source reports it.

## Sources

```{r}
alias_source |> select(source, title, coverage)
```

Municipalities come from [njmunicipalities](https://github.com/tor-gu/njmunicipalities); ORIs
from the FBI [Crime Data Explorer](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/) agency lists.
